comparison: Perfect agreement on confidence-compulsivity relationship (C40-C63, C90-C91). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with strong evidence. OpenEval emphasizes statistical robustness across multiple operationalizations; peer review notes 'convincing evidence' and 'convergence along all measures strengthens inferences.'

Perfect agreement on reduced reminder-setting in compulsivity (C3, C42, C64-C69, C92). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED despite finding being unexpected. OpenEval notes contradiction with initial hypothesis; peer review acknowledges divergence from clinical OCD samples but accepts validity for transdiagnostic sample.

Perfect agreement on partial mediation analysis (C4, C44-C46, C79-C85, C88-C89, C93). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details bootstrapping procedures and incomplete mediation; peer review explicitly accepts 'only partial mediation had robust evidence, multiple effects may be at play.'

Divergent evaluations on confidence-action interaction null finding (C5, C43, C75-C78, C87, C100). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN citing power limitations and task differences; peer review rates SUPPORTED after additional analyses addressed concerns about learning effects and prediction errors.

Perfect agreement on replication findings and task validation (C52-C56). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation of experimental paradigm; peer review notes task 'replicates several major findings on confidence' and accepts foundational results.

Strong agreement on AD null findings (C70-C74). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate reporting of non-significant effects; peer review implicitly accepts null results as part of overall 'convincing evidence' pattern. Peer review also includes C86 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Perfect agreement on perfectionism speculation (C94-C95). Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes interpretation is plausible but requires empirical validation; peer review describes as 'speculative reasons' that set agenda for future research.

Divergent evaluations on explanations for null interaction effect (C101-C103). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as reasonable explanations citing power issues and recent replication failures; peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting original concerns about task design and treating explanations as speculative rather than established.

Perfect agreement on subclinical vs clinical limitation (C104-C105). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes importance of this caveat for interpretation; peer review explicitly accepts limitation and frames as setting up future research directions. OpenEval also includes C106 not addressed by peer review.

Agreement on exploratory AD null finding (C86). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical reporting; peer review groups with other AD null findings (C70-C74) and implicitly accepts as part of overall pattern.

Minimal overlap on methodological claims (C34-C39, C47-C51, C114-C150). OpenEval extensively evaluates methodology as SUPPORTED; peer review only briefly acknowledges reminder effectiveness (C51) as part of accepting the offloading measure. Most methodological details not explicitly evaluated by peer review.
OpenEval evaluates inference about inadequate memory support risk (C6, C112) as SUPPORTED based on combination of findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific inference.
OpenEval evaluates comparison to Kirk et al. study and transdiagnostic approach value (C96-C98) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this literature comparison.
OpenEval evaluates comparison to Mohr et al. study on underconfidence patterns (C99) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this cross-paradigm comparison.

OpenEval evaluates clinical implication about encouraging reminder use (C113) as UNCERTAIN, noting it extends beyond data without testing interventions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this clinical recommendation.
